subject.title: Question: Publisher verification path for active code plugin contributors?

question: Should ClawHub create a public Verified or vetted-community path for third-party code-plugin publishers, and should that status be publisher-scoped, package-scoped, or unavailable for now?
rationale: This choice defines a public security trust signal for executable community plugins and cannot be safely inferred from existing Official, trustedPublisher, scan, or moderation fields.

options.title: Use the RFC as the policy home
options.body: Keep this issue as author-specific context and make https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2272 the canonical place to decide criteria, scope, revocation, and public wording before implementation.

options.title: Document no public path
options.body: State that community packages remain source-linked plus scanned unless a publisher is staff-marked Official, avoiding a new trust tier for now.

options.title: Pilot a vetted-community path
options.body: Approve a limited package-scoped pilot with explicit security review criteria and separate UI/API semantics from Official status.

recommendation.title: Use the RFC as the policy home
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as author-specific context and make https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2272 the canonical place to decide criteria, scope, revocation, and public wording before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest current-history owner for the official publisher policy and package trust surfaces that this decision would change.
